title: The 5 Windiest Planets, Ranked (Earth Makes the List)

scenes.text: Earth makes this list. Number one has winds faster than sound, with almost no sunlight.
Number five: Earth. A cyclone gust in Australia hit two hundred fifty-three miles an hour.
scenes.label: Earth · 253 mph gust

scenes.text: Number four: Jupiter. Winds around the Great Red Spot top four hundred miles an hour.
scenes.label: Jupiter · 400+ mph

scenes.text: Number three: Uranus. Its winds reach about five hundred sixty miles an hour.
scenes.label: Uranus · 560 mph

scenes.text: Number two: Saturn. Winds at its equator blow about eleven hundred miles an hour.
scenes.label: Saturn · 1,100 mph

scenes.text: Number one: Neptune, the farthest planet from the Sun. Its winds pass twelve hundred miles an hour, faster than sound.
scenes.label: Neptune · 1,200+ mph

description:
The fastest winds measured on each planet: Earth's record gust of 253 mph (408 km/h) at Barrow Island, Australia, in 1996; Jupiter's Great Red Spot, over 400 mph; Uranus, up to about 560 mph (900 km/h); Saturn's equator, about 1,100 mph (500 m/s); and Neptune, over 1,200 mph (2,000 km/h), supersonic by Earth standards.
Venus's cloud-top winds of 300-400 km/h just miss the list, and Mars's are slower still.
Why do you think the coldest, darkest planet has the fastest winds?
first_comment: Neptune gets about 900 times less sunlight than Earth and still has the fastest winds. Which planet would you rank next: biggest storms or longest days?
